subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: If the letters of the word PRISON are permuted in all possible ways and the words thus formed are arranged in dictionary order, then find the rank of the word PRISON.

mark_split.label: Write the letters in alphabetical order
Count the words that come before
Add up and state the rank

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the dictionary rank of PRISON — what you write first, how you count the words before it, and how you finish.
insider_note: Every later block depends on the first line: alphabetical order is I, N, O, P, R, S, and O placed after P shifts every block. After P R is fixed there is no third-place block to add, because I is the smallest letter remaining.

steps.label: Alphabetical order of the letters
steps.margin_note: First mark. Six different letters: I, N, O, P, R, S. No repeats, so every count below is a plain factorial.
steps.memory_tip: Sort first: I, N, O, P, R, S. O comes BEFORE P — placing it after shifts every block.
lines: Letters of PRISON in alphabetical order:
I, N, O, P, R, S

recall.must_convey: That the letters of PRISON are first written in alphabetical order: I N O P R S.
accept: write the letters in alphabetical order I N O P R S
first arrange the letters of PRISON alphabetically
alphabetical order of the letters is I N O P R S
letters ni alphabetical order lo rayali, I N O P R S
sort the letters first, that is what dictionary order means
heard_as: I N O P R S

steps.why: Dictionary order is alphabetical order applied letter by letter. Until the letters are sorted there is no way to say which words come before the given one.
common_mistakes: Writing the letters in the order of the word (P, R, I, S, O, N) instead of alphabetical order.
Placing O after P — O comes before P.

steps.label: Count the words before it
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Three letters (I, N, O) come before P: 5! each. With P fixed, three letters (I, N, O) come before R: 4! each. With P R fixed, I is the smallest so no block; with P R I fixed, N and O come before S: 2! each. With P R I S fixed, N comes before O: 1!.
steps.memory_tip: After P R is fixed there is no block, because I is the smallest letter left. Do not invent one.
lines: Words starting with I, N, O: 3 × 5! = 360
Words starting with PI, PN, PO: 3 × 4! = 72
The next word is PRISON itself.

recall.must_convey: That I, N, O give 3 times 5!, then P I, P N, P O give 3 times 4!, then P R I N and P R I O give 2! each, then P R I S N gives 1, and the next word is PRISON.
accept: three letters before P give three times one twenty, three letters before R give three times twenty four, then PRIN two, PRIO two, PRISN one and then PRISON
three sixty for I N O, seventy two for PI PN PO, two and two for PRIN and PRIO, one for PRISN
fix the letters in turn, three blocks of five factorial, three blocks of four factorial, then two, two, one
I N O tho three into five factorial, PI PN PO three into four factorial, PRIN PRIO rendu, PRISN okati
three sixty plus seventy two plus two plus two plus one before PRISON

steps.why: Every word that starts with a smaller letter comes before the given word, and once the first letter matches the same argument repeats on the second letter. Each line fixes one more letter and counts the arrangements of the rest.
common_mistakes: Counting a block for P R before P R I — I is the smallest remaining letter, so there is no such block.
Forgetting the P R I S N block (1!) before PRISON.
Using 5! = 120 for the P I block — after P and I are fixed only 4 letters remain, so it is 4! = 24.

steps.label: Add up and state the rank
steps.margin_note: Last mark. 360 + 72 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 437 words come before PRISON, so its rank is 438.
steps.memory_tip: 437 words come before PRISON, so the rank is 438. Keep both single-word terms.

recall.must_convey: That the counts are added and one is added for the word itself, giving rank 438.
accept: add three sixty, seventy two, two, two, one and one to get four hundred thirty eight
the rank is four thirty eight
four hundred thirty seven words come before it so the rank is four thirty eight
anni add chesi plus one cheste four hundred thirty eight
three sixty plus seventy two plus four plus one plus one is four thirty eight

steps.why: The rank is the position of the word, so it is the number of words before it plus one for the word itself. Forgetting the plus one gives the count of earlier words, not the rank.
common_mistakes: Answering 437 — the count of words before PRISON, not its rank.
Dropping one of the two single-word terms (the PRISN block and PRISON itself).
